neighbours.label: ' of' after a noun for a set arrangement or offer, introducing what it consists of or amounts to (a rate of $15, a curriculum of modules, a plan of care), as opposed to ' of' after an event nominalization (the - pole: derivation of, development of)
fire: The club gives students a reduced rate of five dollars per visit.
New nurses complete a fixed curriculum of online lessons in their first month.
The insurer quoted us a yearly rate of nine hundred dollars.
Each patient leaves the ward with a written plan of care.
The school follows a national curriculum of twelve core subjects.
The bank offered her a fixed rate of four percent for five years.
Volunteers follow a short program of training videos before they start.
The clinic uses a standard course of six weekly sessions.
quiet: The report traces the development of the club over fifty years.
New nurses witnessed the replacement of the old ward by a modern wing.
The insurer is a friend of my uncle.
Each patient remembers the arrival of the new doctor.
The mayor of the town opened the school.
The collapse of the bank shocked the whole region.
Volunteers celebrated the completion of the bridge.
The roof of the clinic was repaired in the spring.

notes: Top 32 are ' of' x29. The - pole fires on nominalizations before 'of' (derivation, survival, development, replacement), so the two poles seem to split kinds of 'of'-phrase. Probe: rate of 0.37, curriculum of 0.46, mix of 0.22, possibility of 0.19, diet of 0.18, cries of 0.17, fee of 0.09; development of 0.02, replacement of 0.07, king of 0.02, cup of 0.04. Activations are modest, so the median may fall short.
